title: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia (ONH): A Comprehensive Clinical Atlas
summary: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia is a congenital, non-progressive optic disc anomaly characterized by a subnormal number of optic nerve axons. It serves as a critical systemic marker often associated with midline brain defects and endocrine dysfunction.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: ONH results from a reduced number of retinal ganglion cell axons. It is thought to arise from an insult during the early second trimester (weeks 6-13 of gestation). Pathologically, there is an increase in fibrous astrocytes and connective tissue in the optic nerve head, leading to a small, pale neuroretinal rim and a variable peripheral halo.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: Step 1: Dilated Fundus Exam: Evaluate for 'Double-ring sign' (peripapillary scleral ring).
Step 2: Pediatric Assessment: Evaluate for Nystagmus, Strabismus, and Refractive Errors (usually high hyperopia/astigmatism).
Step 3: MRI Brain/Orbit: Mandatory to rule out Septo-optic dysplasia (De Morsier syndrome) - check for absent septum pellucidum.
Step 4: Endocrine Panel: Serum GH, TSH, ACTH, and Cortisol levels to rule out hypopituitarism.
Step 5: Visual Field Testing: If patient age permits, look for generalized depression or cecocentral scotomas.

sections.title: Systemic Associations
content: Midline brain defects (Agenesis of Corpus Callosum)

rows: Inner ring marks the termination of retina; outer ring is the scleral canal
Significantly reduced disc area; disc-to-macula ratio < 0.25
Thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL)

sections.title: Red Flags: Emergency Considerations
content: Hypoglycemic seizures in infants (Adrenal crisis/GH deficiency)
Bilateral involvement associated with significant neurodevelopmental delay
Sudden deterioration of vision or unexplained nystagmus
Signs of increased intracranial pressure due to associated hydrocephalus

content.explanation: O (Optic disc small), N (Nystagmus), H (Hyperopia/Hypopituitarism). Always check the hormones if ONH is found!

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: ONH is the most common congenital optic disc anomaly.
Visual acuity ranges from 20/20 to NLP; poor correlation with disc size.
Early MRI is diagnostic gold standard for systemic associations.
Management is multidisciplinary (Pediatric ophthalmology, Endocrinology, Neurology).
